body.en: EST II trigonometry goes beyond right-triangle ratios to include the unit circle, radian measure, graphing, and trigonometric identities.

note.en: EST II works in radians: a full turn is \(2\pi\approx6.28\), not \(360°\). \(P=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\) as above.

body.en:
Graphs of trigonometric functions

The function \( y=A\sin(Bx+C)+D \) has amplitude \( |A| \), period \( \dfrac{2\pi}{B} \), phase shift \( -C/B \), and vertical shift \( D \). Knowing how to read these parameters from a graph or equation is a core EST II skill.

Unit circle: \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\). Key identities: \(\tan\theta = \sin\theta/\cos\theta\); \(\sec\theta = 1/\cos\theta\). Double angle: \(\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta\); \(\cos 2\theta = 1-2\sin^2\theta\). Law of cosines: \(c^2 = a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C\). Area: \(\tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C\).

label.en: Worked example — Non-right triangle (Law of Sines)

body.en:
In triangle \(ABC\): \(a=8\), \(B=35°\), \(C=75°\). Find side \(b\).

\(A = 180°-35°-75° = 70°\). By sine rule: \(\dfrac{b}{\sin B} = \dfrac{a}{\sin A} \Rightarrow b = \dfrac{8\sin 35°}{\sin 70°} \approx \dfrac{4.589}{0.9397} \approx 4.88\).

caption.en: Sinusoidal wave \(y = 2\sin(2x) + 1\) with amplitude \(A = 2\), period \(T = \frac{2\pi}{B} = \pi \approx 3.14\), and midline \(y = 1\).

label.en: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Trigonometry & Angle Measures

body.en:
• Radian vs. Degree Calculator Mode: EST II problems frequently present angles in radians (e.g., \(5\pi/6\)) alongside degree options or vice versa. Always check your calculator's active mode before computing numerical values.
  • Double-Angle Identity Selection: \(\cos(2\theta)\) has three identities: \(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta\), \(2\cos^2\theta - 1\), and \(1 - 2\sin^2\theta\). In equations containing \(\sin\theta\), choose \(1 - 2\sin^2\theta\) to produce a single-variable quadratic in sine; in equations containing \(\cos\theta\), choose \(2\cos^2\theta - 1\).
  • Quadrant Signs (ASTC Rule): Remember: All positive in Q I; Sine positive in Q II; Tangent positive in Q III; Cosine positive in Q IV. For \(\sin\theta = -1/2\), the solutions lie strictly in Quadrants III and IV.
  • Range of Inverse Trigonometric Functions: Standard principal value ranges: \(\arcsin x \in [-\pi/2, \pi/2]\), \(\arccos x \in [0, \pi]\), and \(\arctan x \in (-\pi/2, \pi/2)\). Calculator evaluations will return only the principal value.

question.en: Solve the trigonometric equation \(2\cos^2\theta + 3\sin\theta - 3 = 0\) for all solutions in the interval \(0 \le \theta < 2\pi\).

solution.en:
Use Pythagorean identity: Substitute \(\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta\): \[ 2(1 - \sin^2\theta) + 3\sin\theta - 3 = 0 \implies 2 - 2\sin^2\theta + 3\sin\theta - 3 = 0. \] Multiply by \(-1\): \[ 2\sin^2\theta - 3\sin\theta + 1 = 0 \implies (2\sin\theta - 1)(\sin\theta - 1) = 0. \]

Case 1: \(2\sin\theta - 1 = 0 \implies \sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\). In \([0, 2\pi)\), sine is positive in Quadrants I and II with reference angle \(\pi/6\): \[ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6},\quad \theta = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}. \]

Case 2: \(\sin\theta - 1 = 0 \implies \sin\theta = 1\). In \([0, 2\pi)\): \[ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}. \]

The complete solution set is \(\left\{ \dfrac{\pi}{6},\, \dfrac{\pi}{2},\, \dfrac{5\pi}{6} \right\}\).
